slides.title: Recovering the Calls the Workflow Lost
slides.subtitle: Cora Recap Engine  ·  an operational AI system
slides.caption: A voice call could finish while the event saying so never arrived. The pipeline did not know.

slides.title: The failure was silence.
slides.subtitle: A completed launch, no completion event, no result on the lead.
slides.caption: In late April a burst of calls overwhelmed event delivery. The calls happened. The pipeline lost track of what they produced.

slides.title: The first repair was a script.
slides.subtitle: An engineer replayed affected contacts from a CSV, two days running.
slides.caption: It worked, it did not scale, and it left nothing an operator could see the next morning.
A completed launch with no completion event is a failure. The panel lists each one with four ways to resolve it.
A recovered result is fetched from the source, normalised with the worker's own logic, and replayed through the same pipeline as a live event.

slides.title: Replay cannot do the work twice.
slides.subtitle: A unique key on call events, and an audit row every path reads.
slides.caption: A replay of an event that did arrive reuses the existing record, and a resolved case is not recovered or alerted again.
The dashboard card carries the delivery percentage, so a quiet system and a lost event no longer look the same.

rows: recovery paths, from none in the product
test cases exercise the recovery behaviour, in 4 files
slides.caption: Five ways to recover a lost event where there had been a script, built in five days, with the automatic path under test.

slides.title: What the repository does not prove.
slides.subtitle: No count of events lost or recovered is persisted.
slides.caption: This record measures the mechanism, not the outcome. The audit table could answer that with one query; nobody has run it yet.
